deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no derivation. It is a laboratory register, 'Register über die Kraft der Magnetstäbe' (register of the strength of the magnet bars). It records repeated determinations of a magnetic-strength figure for bars numbered 1–6 and a bar 'B'; in the lower block the bars run 1–8.

The previous page (f.175) derives the static moment of the magnetic force by Gauss's oscillation method. It uses M + (1/2) p r^2 = (𝔐 m t^2 l)/π^2 and the relation A + r^2 = B t^2. Here t is the oscillation period with weights p at distance r. A (moment of inertia term) and B are fitted by least squares from four (r, t) pairs. The numbers on this page are presumably the resulting magnetism figures for each bar on each date. They are probably a product proportional to the magnetic moment times the horizontal intensity, or the moment in Gauss's working units. The page does not say which, so this reading is mine.

Structure of the register:
(a) Faint early entries (Mar 24, Jun 8, a second June date, Jul 10, Jul 24, Aug 1, Aug 3). These show steady loss of magnetism. Bar 1 falls 1818 → 1672 → 1644 → 1620 → 1593. Bar 4 falls 1653 → 1489 → 1376. Bar 5 falls 1979 → 1924 → 1918 → 190x → 1878. Bar 6 falls 1941 → 1887 → 1884 → 1834.
(b) Aug 7: a first line (1620.4, 1562.1, …, 1836.6) consistent with the decayed state. It is followed by a higher line (1700.0, 1712.3, 1725.7, 1497.5, 2049.0, 2054.3). This is evidently after re-magnetisation by stroking ('Streichen'); the next folio explicitly records 'Dch' (Doppelstrich), 'mit 4/8 Stäben gestrichen', 'nach Erwärmung' and 'nach der Trennung'.
(c) Aug 8–17: daily re-measurements showing slow decay after remagnetisation. Bar 1 goes 1743.7 → 1725.1 → 1728.6 → 1716.6 → 1718.2 → 1707.9 → 1627.7 → 1640.8. A drop on Aug 15 coincides with a drop in bar 3 (1716.1 → 1620.2). A value 1597.1 for bar B appears on Aug 14, and a circled marginal note gives B = 2666.8 on 30 Sept.
(d) A new block for 8 bars (dates 20–27, presumably later in August). Bars 7 and 8 are added at about 2170–2317 and decay to about 2030–2065 within days. There are further remagnetisation steps: underlined value sets, for example bar 7 1945.1 → 1983.1 → 2059.3 → 2065.7 and bar 8 → 2109.0 → 2172.3. A final line on the 27th shows large drops for bars 2–4 (1375.1, 1236.6, 1325.8). This presumably follows some operation such as separating bars or a different stroking, continued on f.177 (27: 738.7, 477.4, 307.0 …).

The purpose is empirical study of how permanent the magnetism of steel bars is, and how effective different magnetisation procedures are. This matters for the absolute-intensity method of 1832, because the bar moment must stay constant between the oscillation and deflection experiments.

Illustrative relative losses (my computation): bar 1 lost about 12.4% from Mar 24 to Jul 24 (1593/1818 ≈ 0.876). Bar 4 lost about 16.8% by the second June date (1376/1653 ≈ 0.832). The Aug 7 restroking raised bar 5 by about 10.5% (2049.0/1853.5 ≈ 1.105).
errors: No computations on the page to check; it is a data log. Some entries are unclear or overwritten: a struck 1878 in column 5, a struck 1834 in column 6 rewritten on the Aug 3 line, and a struck entry on line 25 in columns 2–3. These are corrections in the record, not mathematical errors.

results.what: Time series of measured magnetic strength (moment) of individual steel bars, showing secular decay and the effect of remagnetisation (stroking, double touch)
results.modern_name: Magnetic aging / ageing of permanent magnets; stability of magnetic moment; magnetisation by the double-touch method
results.usually_credited_to: Systematic absolute measurements of bar moments: Gauss (1832, Intensitas vis magneticae terrestris) and Gauss–Weber in the Göttingen Magnetic Observatory; stroking methods go back to Michell/Canton/Aepinus (18th c.)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine experimental register from Gauss's well-documented 1832–34 geomagnetic work, in which he discussed the variability of bar magnetism. It adds unpublished raw data but no new mathematics.

checkable.asserts: Bar 1 retained about 0.876 of its March 24 value by Jul 24 (about 12.4% loss).
Bar 4 retained about 0.832 of its March value by the second June measurement.
Remagnetisation on Aug 7 raised bar 5 by about 10.5%.
Bar 1 lost about 2% between the post-stroking Aug 9 value and Aug 14.

transcription_corrections: Column 5, Jul 10: the entry reads '190' plus an illegible final digit (likely 190x, between 1918 and 1878), not a complete number.
Aug 9 block: 1984.8 (column 6) stands above 1987.4 as a separate measurement. The Aug 9 row has dashes in columns 1–4 and values 2007.4 and 1987.4 in columns 5–6.
The value 1597.1 on the Aug 14 line stands in the 'B' column, i.e. it belongs to bar B.
Circled marginal note reads 'B 2666.8 30 Sept' plus a trailing illegible mark (possibly a year); the next page's margin gives 2669.18, so the reading is uncertain.
Bar 8, line 24: the overwritten value appears to be 2057.5 written over another figure.
Bottom line, column 5: '2142.2' with '2087.4' written beneath it.
